name: HubSpot
scope_notes: Private-app and newer developer-platform static authentication coexist. SSO requires eligible Professional/Enterprise subscriptions.

controls.name: App governance: Approve apps
controls.what: Marketplace apps must be approved by a Super Admin before non-admin users can install them; users submit requests.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > select app > Approve
controls.quote: Non-admin users must request access to apps that haven’t been approved yet.

controls.name: App governance: Limit installation (Install Permissions)
controls.what: Restricts which users/teams may install an approved app (Admins, specific users/teams, or everyone).
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Manage access > Install Permissions
controls.quote: Limit installation : control which users and teams can install each app.

controls.name: App governance: Customize optional data permissions
controls.what: Turns optional scopes on or off for an approved app for all users; required scopes cannot be removed.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Approve / Manage access > data permissions
controls.quote: Customize optional data permissions : allow or restrict optional permissions for each approved app.

controls.name: App governance: Revoke approval
controls.what: Removes the app from approved apps and uninstalls it for every user.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Manage access > Revoke Approval
controls.quote: Revoking approval for an app will uninstall it for all users who have previously installed it.

controls.name: Uninstall an app for a specific user
controls.what: Uninstalls an approved app from one user's install; the user can reinstall unless approval is revoked.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Manage access > Installed by > Uninstall
controls.quote: The user can re-install the app in the future. If you want to restrict them from installing, you can revoke approval instead.

controls.name: User permission: App Marketplace access
controls.what: Only Super Admins and users with this permission (plus matching scope permissions) can install apps.
controls.setting: Settings > Users & Teams > user > permissions (Settings access)

controls.name: Deselect optional scopes at install
controls.what: The installing user can clear optional scopes before connecting the app.
controls.quote: You can also clear any of the checkboxes under *Optional scopes* for any permissions that you don't want to grant to the app.

controls.name: User permission: Developer tools access
controls.what: Controls which non-Super Admin users can access developer features; creating service keys requires it.
controls.setting: Settings > Users & Teams > user > permissions (Settings access)
controls.quote: Developer tools access : toggle the Developer tools access switch on to let the user access and manage developer features

controls.name: Service key scopes
controls.what: Each key gets only the scopes selected, and only scopes the creating user already has; editable later.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Service Keys (or Development > Keys > Service Keys) > key > Edit
controls.quote: A key can only be granted scopes the creating user already has

controls.name: Service key Rotate / Delete
controls.what: Rotate creates a new key and expires the old one now or in 7 days; Delete removes the key.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Service Keys > key > Rotate / Delete
controls.quote: If your key is compromised and you want to immediately revoke access, click **Rotate and expire now**.

controls.name: Legacy private app scopes
controls.what: Super Admin selects which scopes the private app token can use; editable after creation.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Scopes / Edit app
controls.quote: select the **checkbox** for each scope you want your private app to be able to access.

controls.name: Legacy private app token Rotate
controls.what: Issues a new token and expires the old one immediately or after 7 days; Super Admins get a reminder after 180 days without rotation.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Auth > Rotate
controls.quote: If your token is compromised and you want to immediately revoke access, click **Rotate and expire now**.

controls.name: Delete legacy private app
controls.what: Deleting the app permanently revokes its access token.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Auth > Delete
controls.quote: When you delete one of your private apps, its access token will be permanently revoked and you'll no longer be able to use it to make API calls.

controls.name: Static auth token view/rotate restricted
controls.what: Only Super Admins or users with a developer seat on the account can view or rotate the static token.
controls.quote: To view or rotate your access token, you must be a super admin or have a developer seat for the associated account.

controls.name: Developer API key deactivate/regenerate
controls.what: The single per-account developer API key can be deactivated and replaced at any time.
controls.quote: You can deactivate your API key and generate a new one at any time.

controls.name: Super Admin required for private apps
controls.what: Only Super Admins can access and create private apps, so withholding Super Admin removes the ability; there is no account-wide off switch.

no_control.what: Required data permissions (scopes) of an app cannot be turned off by the admin.
no_control.quote: Required data permissions for apps cannot be modified or turned off.

controls_unknown: No IP allowlist for API calls found; "Allowed login IPs" (Settings > Security > Login) is documented only for logins.
Whether app governance (approval) covers privately distributed OAuth apps and static-auth apps, or only HubSpot Marketplace listings.
No admin-set token lifetime or mandatory rotation policy found for private app tokens, static tokens, service keys or the developer API key (only manual rotation and reminders).
No account-wide switch found to block service key creation other than withholding Developer tools access / Super Admin.

authentication.summary: Static access token for a legacy (non-project) private app, sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. HubSpot implements it on top of OAuth, so client libraries accept it as an access token.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Trusted-IP documentation restricts account logins; API-call enforcement for private-app/OAuth tokens was not established.

renewal.summary: Rotate the private-app token explicitly, immediately or with a 7-day transition.

administration.summary: Super admins manage legacy private apps: scope selection, viewing and rotating the token, 30-day API call logs, and deletion (which revokes the token). Super admins get rotation emails and a reminder after 180 days without rotation. Removing the user who created the app can make some calls fail until the token is rotated.
administration.conditions: UI creation of new legacy private apps is disabled on 2026-09-28 for accounts created on or after that date and on 2026-10-26 for older accounts; existing legacy private apps keep working. HubSpot points new in-account integrations to service keys (hubspot-5). Migrating a non-project legacy private app to platform 2026.09 is not currently supported. Up to 20 private apps per account.

offboard.details: Removing the user who created the private app makes some (not all) API calls with its token fail.

inventory.details: Super admins see private apps under Development > Legacy apps; GET /account-info/v3/api-usage/daily/private-apps reports usage for all private apps.

reads.ui: Development > Legacy apps > {private app} > Logs tab; Method = GET, search request URL '/crm/v3/objects/contacts'; Export logs (CSV) for 30 days

offboard.ui: Settings > Users & Teams > {user} > Actions > Deactivate user, then Actions > Remove from account

token_format.notes: Static bearer token, does not expire unless rotated. Prefix not shown in fetched private-app docs (service keys use pat-na1-). GitHub secret scanning covers 'Hubspot Private Apps User Token'.

log_sources.notes: Enterprise only. User actions incl. CRITICAL_ACTION subcategories. Records HubSpot-user actions, not API calls.

log_sources.name: Private app Logs tab (API call logs)
log_sources.notes: Per-app API calls for 30 days; filter by method/response/URL; CSV export. No request body, URL params or response payload for successful calls.

credential_id_fields.notes: Private app ID on PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW (also in infoUrl /private-apps/{hubId}/{appId}/auth)
Private app ID on CRITICAL_ACTION / PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW
Maps a found token to its private app, plus userId (creator), hubId, scopes

lifecycle_events.notes: A user revealed the token in the UI (security activity type / audit subCategory). Possible exfil point.

anomaly_cues: PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW by a user who does not own the integration, or from a new country/IP
Token view followed within hours by API calls in the Logs tab from new patterns (new endpoints, export-heavy reads)
Private app whose creator was removed (calls failing with USER_DOES_NOT_HAVE_PERMISSIONS) yet still active
Token not rotated in 180+ days (HubSpot reminder emails)
Scopes broadened on a private app with no change ticket

containment.steps: Private app > Auth > Rotate > 'Rotate and expire now'; or delete the private app (token permanently revoked). Then update the integration with the new token.
containment.notes: 'Rotate and expire later' leaves the old token valid for 7 days; use expire now for incidents.

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for project-based apps (and existing legacy public apps) installed in multiple accounts. The app exchanges the code for a 30-minute access token, sent as a Bearer token, and a refresh token.

federation.details: General CRM API federation is not established. Client credentials documented for selected developer-platform functions is not a general CRM grant.

ip_restriction.boundary: Trusted-IP documentation restricts account logins; API-call enforcement for private-app/OAuth tokens was not established.

renewal.summary: Use the refresh token to get a new 30-minute access token. HubSpot describes refresh tokens as not expiring for now; they stop working when the app is uninstalled or the token is revoked.

administration.summary: Scopes (required, conditionally required, optional) are declared in app-hsmeta.json; installers must be super admins or have HubSpot Marketplace access plus the matching permissions. The client secret can be rotated from the app's Auth tab. Apps on 2026.09 can opt into user-level access (isUserLevel), which limits API access to the installing user's permissions; by default access is account-wide.
administration.conditions: Privately distributed OAuth apps install in up to 10 allowlisted accounts; marketplace apps up to 25 before listing. Creation of legacy public apps ended on 2026-06-23; existing ones keep working. User-level access requires OAuth and a new app (account-level apps cannot be converted).

inventory.details: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps lists connected and approved apps, not individual tokens.

expiry.api: Read expires_in from POST /oauth/v1/token response, or GET /oauth/v1/access-tokens/{token} (returns expires_in)

reads.ui: (App developer account) Development > Legacy apps > {app} > Monitoring > API calls tab; filter method GET and request URL

token_format.notes: Access token opaque, 30-minute lifetime (expires_in 1800). Refresh token example format 'na1-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee' (region prefix like na1-). Client id/secret are GUID-style.

authentication.summary: Bearer access token for a project-based app configured with auth type static and private distribution in app-hsmeta.json. The token appears on the app's Distribution tab after install.

federation.details: Static token tied to a single installed account; no external identity exchange is documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: HubSpot's trusted-IP setting limits account logins (Starter, Professional or Enterprise; Super Admin). Its effect on API calls with static auth tokens is not documented.

lifetime.summary: Static; expiry not documented (rotation every 6 months recommended)

renewal.summary: The token is reused for API calls and rotated from the Distribution tab; whether the old token is invalidated immediately is not documented.

administration.summary: Scopes are declared in app-hsmeta.json; scope changes require reinstalling. Only super admins or users with a developer seat on the account can view or rotate the token.
administration.conditions: Installs in 1 standard account at a time plus up to 10 developer test accounts. Static auth apps cannot use user-level access. Distinct from legacy private app tokens (hubspot-1), whose UI creation HubSpot disables in Sept/Oct 2026, and from account service keys (hubspot-5), which are not tied to an app.

inventory.details: Apps are listed on the Development > Projects page; the token is shown per app on its Distribution tab, with no org-wide token list.

token_format.notes: Static bearer token for a project app with static auth and private distribution; shown on the app's Distribution tab after install. Format not documented in fetched docs.

authentication.summary: Account-level API key created in Development > Keys > Service keys (also shown under Settings > Integrations > Service Keys), with selected object scopes. It is sent as a Bearer token and only authenticates REST API requests, not webhooks, UI extensions or other app features.

federation.details: Static account key created in the HubSpot UI; no external identity exchange is documented for service keys.

ip_restriction.boundary: HubSpot's trusted-IP and allowed-location settings limit account logins (Starter, Professional or Enterprise; Super Admin). The service key docs and launch posts do not mention any source-IP control for API calls made with a service key.

lifetime.summary: No expiry documented; rotation or deletion ends access

renewal.summary: The key is reused until rotated or deleted; rotation can expire the old key immediately or after a 7-day overlap, which can be ended early or cancelled (cancelling revokes the new key).

administration.summary: Super admins and users with the Developer tools access permission can create, edit (name and scopes), rotate and delete service keys and view their request logs. Keys use the developer-platform scope list, are not tied to an individual user, and key values are visible only to admins by default.
administration.conditions: Announced as the replacement for UI-created legacy private apps for in-account integrations; legacy private app creation is disabled on 2026-09-28 (new accounts) and 2026-10-26 (existing accounts). Subject to the same rate limits as privately distributed apps (tiers listed from Free to Enterprise); no separate plan requirement is documented. Separate from project-app static auth tokens (hubspot-3).

offboard.details: Service keys are account-level and keep working after the creator leaves.

inventory.details: All keys are listed at Development > Keys > Service Keys (also Settings > Integrations > Service Keys).

reads.ui: Development > Keys > Service keys > {key} > View logs

token_format.notes: Doc example: 'Bearer pat-na1-*********-****-****-****-************'. 'na1' is likely a region segment (other regions unconfirmed). Same pat- prefix family as HubSpot personal access keys is not confirmed.
